owner: Civilian-harm research team / voluntary NGO partners
ask: Publish a dated, sourced civilian-impact brief and correct evident data errors.
mechanism: Shared factual baseline for diplomacy and humanitarian prioritization.
gate: Public-source only; protect survivor privacy and verification standards.
measure: Cited corrections and independently confirmed protection gaps.
stop: Remove claims when primary evidence fails; do not publish sensitive locations.
cost: Low for desk research; uncertain staffing.

owner: DoD public liaison / legal-policy staff, subject to authorization
ask: Audit existing public civilian-harm procedures and create an accountable referral map.
mechanism: Direct problems to proper government or humanitarian mechanisms.
gate: DoD policy approval; do not pretend official intake.
stop: Stop if a proposed referral compromises neutrality or exposes personal data.

ask: Review existing end-use and supplier integrity controls for authorized defense assistance.
mechanism: Discourage unlawful diversion without obstructing legitimate defense.
gate: Acquisition counsel, legal scope, exporter protections.
measure: Documented audit completion and verified discrepancies resolved.
stop: Suspend speculative referrals; preserve due process.

ask: Coordinate non-sensitive energy, water and medical restoration gaps with Ukrainian consent.
mechanism: Reduce harm and the pressure created by infrastructure attacks.
gate: Host consent, humanitarian independence and deconfliction requirements.
measure: Restored service days, verified civilian access, outage duration.
stop: Pause when shared data could reveal critical vulnerabilities.

owner: Diplomats with UN/OSCE consultation; states must consent
ask: Design a pilot reciprocal energy and civilian-infrastructure non-attack arrangement.
gate: Explicit parties’ acceptance; no implied military enforcement mandate.
measure: Independent incident reviews and service interruptions.
stop: No unilateral sanctions relief before verified response.

owner: Independent monitoring body authorized by parties
ask: Establish protected incident-intake and adjudication rules for a limited truce.
mechanism: Separate deliberate violations, misidentification, accidents and disputed allegations.
gate: Access, mandate, security, confidentiality, data standards.
measure: Time to acknowledge and adjudicate incidents; reversals and corrections.

ask: Develop monitored general ceasefire with security safeguards and reciprocal conditionality.
mechanism: Make renewed aggression less attractive and breaches observable.
gate: Mutual consent, legal review, ceasefire scope and enforcement accountability.
measure: Verified compliance, humanitarian access, POW and missing-person progress.
stop: Escalate violations through agreed lawful dispute process; preserve civilian access.

owner: Ukraine, affected communities, donor governments, auditors
ask: Support civilian-led repair, demining, accountable reconstruction and non-recurrence institutions.
mechanism: Lower long-run instability, empower return and support durable security.
gate: Sovereignty, public procurement audit, affected-population voice.
measure: Safe return, verified cleared land, school/water uptime, grievance remedy.
stop: Halt projects with unresolved displacement, corruption or environmental harm.
